Control your **Intex PureSpa** (Wi-Fi models) from Gladys: power, heating,
filtration, bubbles, jets, salt sanitizer, target temperature, and read the
water temperature and the error codes of the control panel.

The integration talks **directly** to the Wi-Fi module of the spa on your
local network (TCP port 8990). No Intex account, no cloud: it keeps working
without Internet.

## Compatible spas

Intex PureSpa models with built-in Wi-Fi, controlled by the **Intex** app
(formerly "Intex Spa"):

- PureSpa Bubble models with Wi-Fi control;
- PureSpa Jet & Bubble models with Wi-Fi control — tick _My spa has hydro
  jets_;
- models with the built-in salt water system — tick _My spa has a salt
  sanitizer_.

Spas without Wi-Fi are not supported.

## Before you start

1. Connect the spa to your Wi-Fi with the Intex app, as the manual explains.
2. In your router, give the spa a **fixed IP address** (DHCP reservation).
   The integration finds the spa by this address.
3. Gladys must be on the same network as the spa (or able to reach it on
   TCP port 8990). Gladys **5.3** or newer is required.

## Configuration

In Gladys: **Integrations → Intex PureSpa → Configuration**.

| Field                       | What to type                                                         |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Spa address                 | The IP address of the spa, e.g. `192.168.1.50`.                      |
| TCP port                    | Leave `8990`.                                                        |
| My spa has hydro jets       | Ticked on Jet & Bubble models: adds a _Jets_ switch.                 |
| My spa has a salt sanitizer | Ticked on models with a salt system: adds a _Salt sanitizer_ switch. |
| Refresh interval (s)        | How often the spa is read. 60 s by default, 30 s minimum.            |

Save, then click **Test the connection**: the answer shows the water
temperature, the target and the heater state read from the spa.

Then open the **Discover** tab and add the _Intex PureSpa_ device.

## The device

| Feature            | Type                | Notes                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Power              | Switch              | Turns the whole spa on or off.                    |
| Filtration         | Switch              | The pump.                                         |
| Heater             | Switch              | Switching it on also starts the filtration.       |
| Bubbles            | Switch              |                                                   |
| Jets               | Switch              | Only with _My spa has hydro jets_.                |
| Salt sanitizer     | Switch              | Only with _My spa has a salt sanitizer_.          |
| Water temperature  | Temperature sensor  | Not published while the panel shows an error.     |
| Target temperature | Thermostat setpoint | 10–40 °C (or 50–104 °F).                          |
| Error code         | Text                | `OK`, or the code of the panel (`E81`, `E90`...). |

Switching a function **on** while the spa is off powers the spa on first,
as the control panel does.

The spa works in Celsius or Fahrenheit according to its own panel setting:
the integration detects it and the temperatures follow.

## Dashboard widget

Add the **Intex spa** widget to a dashboard. It shows:

- the water and the target temperature, live;
- the state of each function, the connection and the error code;
- buttons: heater, bubbles, filtration on/off, and **Set temperature**, which
  opens a small form.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Spa error detected** — the panel shows an error code. The code is
  available as `{{triggerEvent.data.code}}`.
- **Water temperature reached** — the heater brought the water to the
  target temperature (`temperature`, `target`).
- **Spa no longer answers** — the spa answered, then stopped (power cut,
  Wi-Fi lost...).

To act on a temperature threshold (water below 30 °C...), use the standard
"device state" trigger on the _Water temperature_ feature.

### Actions

- **Heat the spa to** — sets the target temperature and switches the heater
  on (untick _Switch the heater on_ to only change the target). Outputs: water
  temperature, target, heater, error code.
- **Read the spa status** — reads the spa now. Outputs: temperatures, power,
  heater, filtration, bubbles, error code.

Example: "Every Friday at 2 pm, heat the spa to 38 °C", then "When the water
temperature is reached, send me a message".

## Good to know

- The Wi-Fi module of the spa is slow and serves **one client at a time**.
  The integration keeps a single connection open and sends one request at a
  time. The Intex app can be slower to answer while Gladys is connected.
- For the meaning of an error code (E81, E90...), see the manual of your spa:
  the integration passes on the code shown by the panel.
- The integration stores nothing on disk.

## Troubleshooting

- **"The spa does not answer"**: check that the spa is powered, that its Wi-Fi
  light is on, and that the address is right (try `ping` from the Gladys
  machine). If the address changed, set a DHCP reservation.
- **The device badge is red ("unreachable")**: same checks. The badge turns
  back to "local" as soon as the spa answers again.
- **A switch goes back to its old state**: the control panel refused the
  order (a heater during a fault, for example). Look at the error code.
- **Detailed logs**: in Gladys, open the integration logs in **Settings →
  System**.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Intex PureSpa asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration talks to the Wi-Fi module of the spa directly on your network (TCP port 8990): no Intex account, no cloud. First connect the spa to your Wi-Fi with the Intex app, then give it a fixed IP address in your router (DHCP reservation) and type that address below. |
| Spa address | `string` | Yes | IP address (or host name) of the spa's Wi-Fi module on your network. |
| TCP port | `number` | No | Leave 8990, the port of every Intex Wi-Fi module. |
| My spa has hydro jets | `boolean` | No | Hydrojet models only (PureSpa Jet & Bubble). Adds a Jets switch. |
| My spa has a salt sanitizer | `boolean` | No | Models with the built-in salt water system. Adds a Salt sanitizer switch. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the spa is read, in seconds (30 minimum: the Wi-Fi module is slow). |

## How to install Intex PureSpa in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Intex PureSpa appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-intexpurespa:0.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-intexpurespa](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-intexpurespa).

Intex PureSpa requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Intex PureSpa is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
